facts.fact: The Drum's pale pressure seam, which booms, is called the boom line; the ice beside it is thin, and fourteen fingers thick eleven paces to its left.
facts.why: needed because the beat's escape instruction uses the boom line and Ila's earlier soundings.

facts.fact: Captain Raghu is lean, ice-bearded and sleepless, and has met Kunal twice across the Garh Neshar hall; he is bound to Pasang, a grey-wool soldier of about twenty with a brass bell on his shoulder.
facts.why: needed because the beat puts Raghu and Pasang on the page and neither has been described.

facts.fact: Gauri is gagged with cloth, wrists bound before her, and tethered by a cord from her belt to an iron peg driven in the ice beside Dhanu; a scrap of blue wool lies on Dhanu's chest.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Kunal cut her loose.

facts.fact: Kunal's palms blister and split from taking Ila's lie-cold through her foot; Ila's two smallest left toes are dead.
facts.why: needed because the beat sets his blistering hands and her dead toes.

facts.fact: Raghu's loud lie to Pasang, 'The limping one went home this morning', whitens his fingertips; Ila notices, Kunal cannot interpret it.
facts.why: needed because the beat plants clue C17.

facts.fact: Two of Raghu's men, roped as a pair, go through the thin ice by the boom line while chasing Kunal.
facts.why: needed because the beat has the pursuing pair fall through.
